comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

### Mechanism (proven at runtime, not read off the source)

`_spawn_detached_drain` (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:319-333`) calls `subprocess.Popen`
with `**_detach_kwargs()` (`start_new_session=True`) and **no `cwd=`**. A detached child
therefore inherits the parent's working directory and, by design, outlives the parent. This
project's workflow runs ordinary writes from `make worktree` worktrees that are removed
afterwards, so the child routinely ends up holding a working directory that no longer exists.
The first `os.getcwd()` then raises `FileNotFoundError` — for the drain that is
`_config_sources.repo_root`'s final `Path.cwd()` fallback, reached via
`queue.claim` -> `_tracker` -> `config.tracker_dir` -> `load_config` -> `repo_root`. The child
dies BEFORE appending its CLAIM event, so nothing is claimed and nothing drains.

### Discriminating experiment

Two detached spawns, identical in every respect (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`,
same interpreter, same removal of the spawning directory mid-flight), differing ONLY in
whether an explicit `cwd=` was passed:

- **no `cwd=`** -> `CHILD getcwd RAISED: FileNotFoundError [Errno 2] No such file or directory`
- **explicit `cwd=`** -> `CHILD getcwd -> /private/tmp/spitbug`

That rules out the alternatives the shape of the traceback invites — `start_new_session`
itself, `close_fds`, the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, and interpreter startup — since all are
present in the passing control. The sole discriminator is the explicit working directory.

Reproduced again as a unit test that drives the real `_spawn_detached_drain`, removes the
spawning worktree with a real `rmtree`, and reads back what the real child resolved:
`ERR FileNotFoundError` before the fix.

### A detail that shapes the fix

A `make worktree` worktree has its own real `.rebar/`, but its `.tickets-tracker` is a
**symlink** to the canonical store (verified). So the tracker path a detach site is handed may
itself be a path *through* the doomed worktree. Choosing `dirname(tracker)` unresolved would
pin the child to the very worktree it must not depend on — the durable answer is
`dirname(realpath(tracker))`, the canonical store's repo root, with a walk up to the nearest
existing ancestor so the chosen directory is never itself dead.

### The class: this is three sites, not one

A sweep of every detached spawn in `src/rebar` found the identical omission at all three
children that are designed to outlive their parent — none of them passes `cwd=`:

| site | detached | explicit cwd | how it dies |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm/enrich_drain.py:319` `_spawn_detached_drain` | yes | no | `Path.cwd()` in `repo_root` |
| `_store/push.py:209` async `push_tickets_branch` | yes | no | `git` startup under `run_git` |
| `_commands/compact_trigger.py:206` `_spawn_detached_sweep` | yes | no | `git` startup under `run_git_write` |

The other `start_new_session=True` uses in the tree (`grounding/harness.py:176`,
`jira/acli_subprocess.py:443`, `jira_family/wiki_render.py:384`) are NOT detached — the flag
is there only so a timeout can `killpg` the group, and the parent blocks on `communicate()`.
They are correctly out of scope.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect`

Cited contract, in the code's own words: `_spawn_detached_drain` — "Detach a `rebar enrich
--drain` child that **outlives the current command**"; the module docstring — "DETACHES the
enrichment to a child that outlives the command"; `push.py:222` — "orphan it (own session);
**survives parent exit**"; `_spawn_detached_sweep` — "Detach a sweep child that **outlives
this command**". A child that dies at `getcwd()` the moment its parent's directory is removed
does not satisfy any of those. This is not a feature request or intended behaviour.

### Defect origin: `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135` (leggy-heedless-mosquito), class `plan_defect`

`git log -L 318,333:src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` gives exactly one commit for the
implicated lines: `9ad46965bd` (2026-07-09) "feat(overlap): Tier-1 opportunistic detached
drain + rebar enrich CLI", trailer `rebar-ticket: c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135`. No carrier to walk
through, and the date test does not fire: there is no good->bad transition, because the site
was never right — the `cwd` was omitted in the commit that created the spawn. So this is an
omission at birth, and here the fix site IS the cause site.

`plan_defect` rather than `regression`: c1de's plan specified the detach down to its exact
POSIX flags — "POSIX reuses push.py's approach (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`)
+ its PYTHONPATH bootstrap" — and simply never considered the child's working directory. A
reviewer of c1de could plausibly have caught it; that is the escape worth counting.

**Divergence worth recording:** the same plan sentence names `src/rebar/_store/push.py:108`
as the pattern being copied, and push.py has the same omission — introduced by `57114212cf`
(2026-06-12, "feat(tier-d): rebar._store write/sync core", pre-trailer, no
`rebar-ticket:`), with `7480964ca0` (a repo-wide `ruff format`) as a pure carrier on top.
`compact_trigger`'s copy came later still, from `d2dea317ec` (2026-08-13, ticket
`1fde-becd-942a-4351`), whose docstring says outright that it "Mirrors
`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain`". So the omission propagated by deliberate imitation
across three tickets. I am still attributing THIS bug to c1de and not to 57114212cf: 5711
created a flawed exemplar, not a contract that c1de was obliged to meet, and the drain's own
defect entered the tree with c1de. The two sibling sites are being fixed in scope under this
ticket rather than attributed separately.

### Caller-dependency gate: clear

`_spawn_detached_drain` has exactly one caller (`maybe_drain`), `_spawn_detached_sweep` one,
and push's spawn is inline in its own async branch. Nothing depends on the child INHERITING
the caller's directory: the drain child re-resolves config (and the store root is the correct
resolution target, reached through the same symlinked tracker), and the push/sweep children
address git explicitly with `git -C <path>` and need a live cwd only for git's own startup.
The existing tests at all three sites stub the spawn helpers, so none pins the absent kwarg.
Only-incidental usage — proceeding to Phase 2.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 2 — fix, RED->GREEN, and replication

### The fix (55 insertions, 0 deletions, 4 files)

New stdlib-only helper `detached_child_cwd(tracker)` in `src/rebar/_proc.py` — already this
repo's documented single source of truth for logic shared between detached-child spawn sites,
and a deliberate leaf with no `rebar.*` imports, which the helper preserves. It returns the
CANONICAL store's repo root: `os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(tracker))`, walked up to the
nearest existing ancestor, ultimately `/`, which cannot be removed. It is total — it never
raises, because all three call sites detach under a never-raise posture.

All three detach sites now pass it as `cwd=`:

- `llm/enrich_drain.py::_spawn_detached_drain` -> `cwd=detached_child_cwd(tracker)`
- `_commands/compact_trigger.py::_spawn_detached_sweep` -> `cwd=detached_child_cwd(tracker)`
- `_store/push.py::push_tickets_branch` (async branch) -> `cwd=detached_child_cwd(base_path)`

`realpath` is the load-bearing part, not tidiness: a provisioned worktree's
`.tickets-tracker` is a SYMLINK into the main checkout, so the UNRESOLVED parent would be the
very worktree we are escaping. Taking the PARENT and not the tracker itself matters too — a
child sitting inside `.tickets-tracker` resolves the repo root to the tracker and then hunts
for a tracker inside the tracker.

Nothing else changed: `_detach_kwargs`, the child command strings, the tracker path passed as
argv, and `_config_sources.repo_root` are all untouched. No test was modified or weakened, and
no new dependency was added (`os` was already imported).

### RED -> GREEN, with a held-out oracle

`tests/unit/test_detached_child_cwd.py` (new, 7 tests) was written and proven RED *before* any
fix existed, then moved OUT of the working tree so the implementing subagent never saw it — it
was given only the contract, never the assertions or the path.

RED, each for the right reason:
- the behavioural test (real `_spawn_detached_drain`, real `rmtree` of the spawning worktree,
  a real child reporting what it resolved) -> `ERR FileNotFoundError`, the production
  traceback reproduced;
- the three per-site tests -> recorded `cwd` is `None` at all three detach sites;
- the three helper tests -> `ImportError`, the helper did not exist.

GREEN: 7/7 pass against the fix the subagent wrote blind.

**Mutation checks — five defect-seeded mutants, all returned the suite to RED**, and restoring
returned it to GREEN:

| seeded defect | result |
|---|---|
| drop `cwd=` from `enrich_drain` | 2 failed |
| drop `cwd=` from `compact_trigger` | 1 failed |
| drop `cwd=` from `push` | 1 failed |
| `realpath` -> `abspath` (stop seeing through the symlink) | 5 failed |
| return the tracker instead of its parent | 6 failed |

Refactoring litmus: the tests assert what a real child process resolves via `os.getcwd()`, and
the `cwd` argument handed to the OS at a real process boundary — plus INVARIANCE across two
different calling directories rather than a literal. No private name, no source grep, so a
rename or a private extraction cannot redden them.

### Replication of the original report, on THIS store

Same scenario as the four production tracebacks: spawn the drain child from a directory whose
`.tickets-tracker` symlinks the canonical store, then `rmtree` that directory while the child
is alive. Two arms, identical but for `cwd=`:

```
[before] spawn cwd=None                       -> child exit=1, drain log grew by 1648 bytes
         FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] ... in _config_sources.py:94  return Path.cwd()
[after]  spawn cwd='/Users/joeoakhart/rebar'  -> child exit=0, drain log grew by 0 bytes
```

The original report no longer reproduces: the child survives the removal of the worktree that
spawned it and completes its drain run cleanly.

### An honest limit on AC "the three wedged entries drain"

They do not, and this fix cannot make them. Chasing that criterion surfaced a SECOND,
independent cause, now filed as `spongy-illjudged-terrier` (569c-931f-69a2-4c1d) and linked
`discovered_from` this ticket: `enrich()` builds an unbounded prompt, and for the three
largest tickets in this store it exceeds the model's context window —

```
prompt is too long: 206826 tokens > 200000 maximum   (400 ValidationException)
```

confirmed by calling `enrich()` directly on `e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2` (fails in 2.8 s). `drain()`
treats that as transient and leaves the claim to lease-expire, so the entry cycles
claimed -> expired -> pending forever. I watched two full cycles twenty minutes apart
(`drainer-41817-1` at 16:02, `drainer-63784-1` at 16:17), neither reaching `done`.

So the premise that this fix alone would silence the gate warning on this store is wrong, and
I would rather say so than tick the box. Both causes must land before `958e`'s "the WARNING no
longer fires on an ordinary write" is observable here. What IS demonstrated is the equivalent
reproduction the AC allows for: a detached drain child spawned from a since-removed worktree
now claims and completes instead of dying.

### Siblings swept

Construct axis: every detached spawn in `src/rebar` — three sites, all with the same omission,
all fixed here. Parity axis: the other three `start_new_session=True` uses
(`grounding/harness.py:176`, `jira/acli_subprocess.py:443`,
`jira_family/wiki_render.py:384`) are NOT detached — the flag is only there so a timeout can
`killpg` the group, and the parent blocks on `communicate()`. Correctly out of scope, and
`cwd=` would change nothing for them.

comments.body:
## Residual risk — dispositions

Three fragilities were observed with citations during this investigation and none is left
undispositioned. All are **ticket filed**, all linked `discovered_from` this bug:

- **`spongy-illjudged-terrier` (569c-931f-69a2-4c1d)** — `enrich()` builds an unbounded
  prompt, so the three largest tickets fail with a 400 (`206826 tokens > 200000 maximum`) and
  cycle claimed -> lease-expired -> pending forever. This is the reason this store's queue is
  still not quiet after the cwd fix, and the reason the
  `enrich drain gate check took ~Nms` warning is still firing here (observed live at 429.6 ms
  and 648.5 ms on two ordinary writes while filing these tickets).
- **`nuclear-calm-heron` (da68-fc7c-068c-4c53)** — from a worktree the tracker resolves to the
  WORKTREE path, so `_rebar_dir` puts the drain advisory lock in the worktree's own
  `.rebar`. Two agents in two worktrees therefore hold two different locks while draining the
  SAME store, which defeats the lock's only purpose. It also explains why the canonical drain
  log holds only four tracebacks for a condition that recurs by design — most of the evidence
  was deleted with the worktrees that produced it, and it accounts for the one log line the
  cwd fix does NOT explain (`Error: cannot list '<worktree>/.tickets-tracker'`).
- **`afeard-technical-kodiakbear` (2dc4-9bcd-75b9-4544)** — the three detach sites are
  copy-paste siblings by their own admission, which is precisely how this one omission reached
  three files across three tickets over two months. One `spawn_detached()` so the next
  property is got right once.

**Accepted, not filed:** `_config_sources.repo_root`'s `Path.cwd()` fallback still raises. I
left it deliberately — a silently-wrong repo root is worse than a loud failure, and the three
detached children no longer reach it now that each gets an explicit cwd. The remaining
exposure is long-lived IN-PROCESS work, which cannot be given its own cwd; that question is
carried in `afeard-technical-kodiakbear`'s scope rather than answered here.

**Gerrit:** change 1974.

comments.body:
## Landed and closed

**Gerrit change 1974 — MERGED** (302 insertions, 0 deletions, 0 unresolved comments).
`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on patch set 2; Gerrit rebased server-side to PS3 and
submitted. CI green across the full matrix — lint + type-check, pytest on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/
3.13 and macos py3.13, the bounded mutation gate, identity, packaging/optionality, artifact
provenance, and pip-audit.

Closed `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135`. Verified afterwards that the
ticket carries exactly ONE `caused_by` edge, so the known duplicate-edge defect did not bite
(`10d0`'s idempotent caused_by write landed on main shortly before this change).

**Patch set 2 exists because of the review.** `LLM-Review` passed PS1 with one advisory
finding: the `except OSError: return os.sep` branch of `detached_child_cwd` was documented
as load-bearing to the never-raise contract but had no test. That was a real gap in my own
oracle — a documented invariant with no test is precisely what rots — so I added
`test_durable_cwd_never_raises_when_the_callers_own_directory_is_gone`, which reaches that
branch the only way it can be reached (a RELATIVE tracker resolved from an already-dead cwd,
sending `realpath` through `getcwd()`). Removing the guard fails that test and only that
test, so the sixth mutant is killed as precisely as the first five.

### AC disposition, stated plainly

- AC 1 (a drain child from a since-removed worktree resolves and drains) — **met**, proven by
  the before/after replication on this store and by the held-out unit test.
- AC 2 — **met via its own "or an equivalent reproduction does" clause**, not by the three
  named entries. Those three are blocked by a second, independent defect
  (`spongy-illjudged-terrier`, 569c-931f-69a2-4c1d): their enrichment prompt exceeds the model
  context window, so they cycle forever. Ticking this box on the equivalent-reproduction clause
  rather than silently implying the named entries drained.
- AC 3 (lint, typecheck, CI pytest green) — **met**.

Anyone tracking `958e`'s "the WARNING no longer fires on an ordinary write": it still fires
on this store (observed at 429.6 ms and 648.5 ms during this session), and it will keep firing
until 569c lands too. That is the honest end state of this ticket, not a regression in it.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain` starts the detached drain child with
`subprocess.Popen([...], env=..., stdin=..., stdout=..., stderr=log_fh, **_detach_kwargs())` —
with **no `cwd=`**. The child therefore inherits the parent's working directory.

rebar's own workflow creates short-lived worktrees and removes them (`make worktree` /
`git worktree remove`). When a write from inside such a worktree spawns a drain child and the
worktree is later removed, the child's inherited cwd no longer exists. `queue.claim` calls
`_tracker(repo_root)` -> `config.tracker_dir` -> `_config_sources.repo_root` -> `Path.cwd()`,
and `os.getcwd()` raises:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

The drain aborts before claiming anything.

## Evidence (2026-08-20, this repo's own store)

`.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log` carries this traceback for **four distinct removed worktrees**:

```
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-ci-latency-debug
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-structured-duplicates
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-zizmor-online
/Users/joeoakhart/split-config-writer
```

The store currently holds **3 permanently pending enrichment entries** that never drain:

```
8625-7bea-67db-4cdc   9305-b42c-3262-4c58   e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2
```

Notably these are also the three largest ticket directories in the store (870 / 747 / 621
event files) — the most re-certified tickets, so the ones most often re-enqueued.

## Why this matters beyond a failed drain

It defeats the fix for `moist-short-lionfish` (958e-f4b3-275c-4154). That bug makes the
write-path drain gate O(1) via a marker recording "nothing can be pending before T". The fast
path is only reachable when the queue is genuinely quiet — correctly so, since a marker must
never be able to hide real work. With entries wedged pending forever, the gate keeps doing the
full O(ticket-count) store walk on every write and the 20 ms budget warning keeps firing, even
with 958e landed. So 958e's acceptance criterion "the WARNING no longer fires on an ordinary
write" is not observable on this store until this is fixed.

## Approach (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Pass an explicit, known-good `cwd` to the detached child rather than inheriting one that may be
gone — the tracker's parent (the repo root) is already computed by `_rebar_dir(tracker)` and is
the natural choice. Consider also whether `_config_sources.repo_root`'s `Path.cwd()` fallback
should degrade rather than raise, since any detached/daemonised caller has the same exposure.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (`_spawn_detached_drain`)
- possibly `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` (`repo_root`'s cwd fallback)
- tests under `tests/unit/`

## Testing
- A test that spawns the drain child from a directory that is removed before the child resolves
  the tracker, and asserts the drain still claims and processes the entry.
- A test pinning that the child is launched with an explicit `cwd` that does not depend on the
  caller's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A detached drain child started from a since-removed worktree still resolves the tracker
      and drains.
- [x] The three wedged entries above drain (or an equivalent reproduction does).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging 958e-f4b3-275c-4154 (moist-short-lionfish) — the reason that bug's fix
cannot be observed end-to-end on this store. Out of that ticket's scope (different file,
different mechanism), filed rather than folded in.

file_impact.reason: new detached_child_cwd helper: the durable working directory a detached child is anchored to
the reported site: _spawn_detached_drain now passes an explicit cwd
sibling detach site with the same omission: async push child now passes an explicit cwd
sibling detach site with the same omission: sweep child now passes an explicit cwd
the RED-first oracle: real child survives removal of its spawning worktree, plus the per-site and helper contracts
